description: s441 fix round 3 (review N2). A handler that awaits a server call calls preventDefault through string-literal bracket access (`event["preventDefault"]()`) after that await. The browser has already submitted the form by then (reviewer-executed: defaultPrevented false on the branch, true on main before the handler became async). Round 2 matched only a direct `event.preventDefault()`; the event is now followed by binding through aliases, bracket access and closures, and the build fails closed. (s457 3a: the handler takes the event as the parameter of a `${(event) => { … }}` listener — a compiler-wrapped handler does not bind `event`, SPEC §5.2.)
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S478 "⭐ RULED — open owner questions, PA recs adopted wholesale" item 10 (g-boot-event-cases-unhandled-server-call-s478)
rationale: §13.2: event control on the handler's event parameter after its first await SHALL be a compile error (E-EVENT-CONTROL-AFTER-AWAIT, §34). (S478 open-Qs ruling item 10: the server call is written as a handled statement — `const ok: bool = isOk(1) !{ _ :> false };` then `@verdict = ok ? … : …;` — since §19.9.10 makes an unhandled client call of a server function E-ERROR-002; the case's point is unchanged.)
